items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: Eddie Durham was in the band, Eddie Tompkins, my brother Keg Johnson, and we had one great hell of a band.

ctx.x: you, now, another proficient man who was a university man from the University of Nebraska, and we made him take the band over. See? So Jesse said he didn't want the band, but we forced it upon him, and he says, 'well now the only way I can do you any good is I have to take you to my hometown,' which he was from Atchison, Kansas, but he had -- where a guy had booked him before, he had what which was called the Blue Serenaders.

So now we've transferred under that name, the Blue Serenaders, Jesse Stone and his Blue Serenaders, out of Saint Joseph, Missouri. And all this time Eddie Durham was in the band, Eddie Tompkins, my brother Keg Johnson, and we had one great hell of a band. And this drummer, John R. Davis --
What town were you out of?

items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: Eddie Thompkins, they all played with Eli Rice after they left Jesse Stone, see?

ctx.x: And he played a little saxaphone too. But anyway, getting back to the first black nightclub, well we had -- we were fortunate enough to get hold of a man by the name of Eddie Thompkins on trumpet, who later played with Jimmy Lunceford and was an outstanding trumpet player, and the rest of the guys --
Now what band is this, Budd?
